density.why: The same property on another specimen or grade

density moulded.why: A printed or filament density can sit a few percent below the resin's

flexural XY.why: Flexural and tensile moduli of a printed bar agree to within about 20%

flexural Z.why: Across the layers a bar is weaker and softer

tensile Z.why: XY is typically about 1.4 times Z

tensile unk.why: Direction not stated; may be a moulded bar

tensile moulded.why: A printed XY bar reaches roughly 85% of a moulded bar's stiffness

tensile XY annealed.why: Annealed after printing: a crystallising matrix stiffens, about 11 % (13 grades that publish both: median x1.11, 1.05 to 1.35; D162)

flexural moulded.why: Moulded flexural modulus, converted as a moulded tensile one

hardness A.why: Shore A through Gent (1958). Printed data-sheet moduli scatter on both sides of it: Gent under-predicts above about 90A (PEBA 90A flexural 80 MPa is 3.8 times Gent).

hardness D.why: Shore D through Qi, Joyce and Boyce (2003). Elastomers only. Printed data-sheet moduli sit below the Gent and Qi hardness relations, and vary with how each lab defines an elastomer's modulus

break XY.why: Break stress sits at or just below the ultimate strength of a filled or brittle bar

yield XY.why: For a thermoplastic that necks, yield is the maximum stress

ultimate Z.why: Across the layers strength is typically 60% of XY, with a wide spread

flexural XY.why: Flexural strength of a printed bar is typically 1.4 to 1.8 times its tensile strength

ultimate moulded.why: A printed XY bar reaches roughly 70 to 85% of a moulded bar's strength

ultimate XY annealed.why: Annealed after printing: about 14 % stronger (10 grades that publish both: median x1.14, 0.93 to 1.27; D162)

yield moulded.why: Moulded yield stress, converted as moulded strength

break Z.why: Across the layers a bar breaks at a fraction of its XY strain

break moulded.why: A printed bar breaks at a small fraction of a moulded bar's strain: nGen prints 11% against 190% moulded

break XY annealed.why: Annealed after printing: a crystallised bar stretches less (13 grades that publish both: median x0.81, 0.33 to 1.50; D162)

yield XY.why: Break strain is never below the yield strain, and a ductile bar goes far beyond it

yield unk.why: Yield strain or strain at maximum stress, direction not stated

HDT 1.8 semi-filled.why: At 0.45 MPa a fibre-filled semicrystalline bar holds about 24 °C longer than at 1.8 MPa

HDT 1.8 semi-unfilled.why: Unfilled semicrystalline bars separate widely between the two loads

HDT 1.8 amorphous.why: Amorphous bars soften over a narrow range near Tg, so the two loads sit close

HDT unstated.why: A heat deflection value without its load is 0.45 MPa or 1.8 MPa; 0.45 MPa is never the lower

Tg amorphous.why: An amorphous bar deflects at 0.45 MPa near its glass transition

Vicat amorphous.why: Vicat softening sits a little above HDT at 0.45 MPa for amorphous polymers

Vicat semi-filled.why: Fibre-filled semicrystalline: Vicat runs well above HDT

Vicat semi-unfilled.why: Unfilled semicrystalline: a needle finds the melt long before a bar deflects

Tm semi-filled.why: A fibre network carries a semicrystalline bar to within about 40 °C of its melting point

HDT 0.45 moulded semicrystalline.why: A printed semicrystalline bar crystallises less than a moulded one and deflects earlier

HDT 0.45 annealed.why: Annealed after printing: a crystallising matrix deflects tens of degrees higher (11 grades that publish both: median +52 C, +28 to +108; D162)

HDT 0.45 moulded amorphous.why: Moulded and printed amorphous bars both deflect near Tg
